## Completion Report

**Branch**: `001-logredact-cli`
**Plan**: `specs/001-logredact-cli/plan.md`

**Generated artifacts**

| Artifact | Contents |
|---|---|
| `plan.md` | Technical Context, Constitution Check (10 gates, all PASS), project structure, Complexity Tracking |
| `research.md` | 10 decisions with rationale and rejected alternatives |
| `data-model.md` | The 4 spec entities mapped to plain Python values, plus the run-outcome table |
| `contracts/cli.md` | Command-line contract: operands, options, stream guarantees, exit statuses, encoding |
| `contracts/redaction-patterns.md` | Recognition grammar with must-match / must-not-match tables |
| `quickstart.md` | 10 runnable validation scenarios + the full FR/SC-to-test matrix |

**Design**: `src/logredact/` with `__main__.py`, `cli.py` (I/O, argparse, exit status), `redact.py` (pure text layer); `tests/` with unit, subprocess-contract, fidelity, performance, and a stdlib-only gate test. Python 3.11+, stdlib only (`re`, `argparse`, `sys`, `io`, `os`, `collections`), pytest via `pyproject.toml` `pythonpath = ["src"]` — no install step.

**Two things worth your attention:**

1. **The spec contradicts itself on `admin@1.2.3.4`** (research item R-000). FR-009 requires an email's final domain label to be "two or more letters", which makes `1.2.3.4` not a domain — so the only match would be the IP, giving `admin@[IP]`. But FR-021 *and* the Edge Cases both state it must produce exactly one `[EMAIL]`. These cannot both hold. I resolved it by letting the email domain also be a valid dotted quad, so the whole address redacts to `[EMAIL]` and the local part isn't left exposed. Consequence: `user@10.0.0.7` now counts as an email, not an IP. Reversing it is one pattern alternative plus a spec amendment.

2. **`argparse.parse_args` would have failed an acceptance scenario.** I verified the design by running it, and plain `parse_args` with `nargs="*"` rejects `logredact a.log --count b.log` with `unrecognized arguments: b.log` — breaking FR-001's "any order". The plan specifies `parse_intermixed_args` instead, verified against all four operand/flag orderings. The redaction core was also executed against every worked example and look-alike in the spec (`99 4111 1111 1111 1111` → `99 [CARD]`, 25-digit run untouched, CRLF/bare-CR/non-UTF-8 round-trip byte-exact) and all matched.

One limitation stated rather than hidden: SC-006's 1 GB figure is verified by a flat-memory measurement plus a `slow`-marked large-input test, not by a 1 GB fixture on every `pytest` run (research item R-008).
